project.name: curl
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace contains separate `curl` and `curl_fuzzer` checkouts at the commits above. The scored locations below are anchored to those exact staged sources, which reproduced the saved ASan crash; Stage 02 did not run the fixed image.

classification.classification_note: The saved sanitizer symptom is `negative-size-param`, but the source-level defect is that `mqtt_publish()` treats libcurl's unspecified-size sentinel `postfieldsize == -1` as a real `size_t` payload length. That signed-to-unsigned conversion makes `payloadlen == SIZE_MAX`, wraps the MQTT packet-size arithmetic, and then drives `memcpy()` from a 1-byte empty-string payload buffer allocated by `fuzz_tlv_to_string()`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42490798 (curl): Negative-size-param found by fuzz target curl_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42490798
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param (size=-1)` in `mqtt_publish()` on the staged vulnerable sources. Direct inspection of the saved 80-byte witness shows a three-record `curl_fuzzer` TLV corpus: TLV 1 sets `CURLOPT_URL` to raw bytes `mqtt:/` followed by eight `0xff` bytes and a trailing `/ ` path segment, TLV 2 stages a 46-byte mock-server reply whose first four bytes are `20 20 00 00`, and TLV 3 sets `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS` with zero-length data. Before any fuzzed option is applied, `Curl_init_userdefined()` initializes `data->set.postfieldsize` to the sentinel `-1`. The TLV 3 `fuzz_tlv_to_string()` call then materializes a 1-byte heap string `""`, and the `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS` setter stores that pointer while switching the request to `HTTPREQ_POST` without touching `postfieldsize`. TLV 1 is materialized into a URL string and stored through the `CURLOPT_URL` setter; `urlapi.c:seturl()` then splits the bytes after `mqtt:/` into eight hostname bytes plus path `/ `, and `curl_url_get(uh, CURLUPART_PATH, &data->state.up.path, 0)` copies that path into transfer state. On the MQTT path, TLV 2's staged reply first makes `mqtt_doing()` read control byte `0x20`, decode remaining-length byte `0x20` to nonzero length 32, and advance into `MQTT_CONNACK`; `mqtt_verify_connack()` then reads `0x00 0x00`, so `mqtt_doing()` dispatches to `mqtt_publish()`. There, vulnerable line 323 casts the still-live sentinel `postfieldsize == -1` directly to `size_t`, so `payloadlen` becomes `SIZE_MAX` instead of `strlen(payload) == 0`; with the staged one-byte topic path, `remaininglength = payloadlen + 2 + topiclen` wraps to 2, `malloc()` returns a 4-byte packet buffer, and the later `memcpy(&pkt[i], payload, payloadlen)` reaches ASan's `negative-size-param` interceptor. The fix in `patch.diff` adds the missing `postfieldsize < 0` handling (and a null-payload guard) before computing `payloadlen`.

evidence_note: Stage 02 used the staged `sample_info.json`, `patch.diff`, `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, `reproduction_report.json`, the saved `poc`, and the staged vulnerable sources under `_work/src`. It also read `trace_feedback.json` and rebuilt the chain to add the `urlapi.c:seturl()` host/path split, the later `curl_url_get(...PATH...)` write into `data->state.up.path`, and the `mqtt_doing()` remaining-length / CONNACK transition plus explicit `readbuf` population before the CONNACK predicate. `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so no extra instrumentation or reruns were performed.

source.description: First project-side parser statement that consumes attacker bytes and decodes TLV 1 into typed URL fields later materialized and stored in libcurl state.
source.value_from: Direct inspection of the saved 80-byte `poc` shows TLV headers `00 01 00 00 00 10`, `00 02 00 00 00 2e`, and `00 05 00 00 00 00`: TLV 1 is `CURLOPT_URL`, length 16, data `mqtt:/\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff/ `; TLV 2 is `RESPONSE0`, length 46, beginning `20 20 00 00`; TLV 3 is `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS`, length 0.

tainted_value_origin.description: The zero-length `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS` TLV decoded from the third record is materialized here as a real heap string. With `tlv->length == 0`, this allocates a 1-byte buffer containing only `\0`, which ASan later identifies as the payload allocation consumed by `mqtt_publish()`.

root_cause.description: Missing negative-size handling. `mqtt_publish()` aliases the payload pointer correctly but casts libcurl's still-live `postfieldsize == -1` sentinel directly to `size_t` instead of treating it as 'unspecified' and deriving `strlen(payload)`. The patch replaces this with a `postfieldsize < 0` branch and only casts nonnegative sizes.

sink.description: ASan sink. By the time this call executes, `payload` still aliases the 1-byte empty string from the third TLV, `payloadlen` is `SIZE_MAX`, and `&pkt[i]` already points past the 4-byte packet allocation created after the wrapped size arithmetic. AddressSanitizer aborts here with `negative-size-param (size=-1)`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged URL has already selected the MQTT handler, the staged RESPONSE0 bytes move `mqtt_doing()` from `MQTT_REMAINING_LENGTH` to `MQTT_CONNACK`, `mqtt_verify_connack()` accepts the following `0x00 0x00` bytes, and the request state is `HTTPREQ_POST`, so execution enters the MQTT publish path instead of the subscribe path.

coarse_trace.summary: Libcurl initializes `data->set.postfieldsize` to the sentinel `-1` before any fuzzed option is applied.
The saved corpus is decoded into TLV 1 URL bytes, TLV 2 `RESPONSE0`, and TLV 3 zero-length `POSTFIELDS`; TLV 1 and TLV 3 are materialized as strings, and TLV 2 is staged as socket 0's first reply.

Libcurl stores the URL and empty payload pointer, leaves `postfieldsize` at its default `-1`, splits `mqtt:/.../ ` into hostname bytes and path `/ `, copies that path into `data->state.up.path`, and copies `HTTPREQ_POST` into live transfer state.
The staged response bytes move `mqtt_doing()` from `MQTT_REMAINING_LENGTH` to `MQTT_CONNACK`, `mqtt_verify_connack()` reads `0x00 0x00`, and the POST arm enters `mqtt_publish()`.
`mqtt_publish()` decodes the one-byte topic, casts the still-live `-1` sentinel to `SIZE_MAX`, wraps the remaining-length arithmetic to 2, and allocates only a 4-byte packet.

Header and topic writes advance the packet cursor past that 4-byte allocation, and the final payload `memcpy()` is invoked with `payloadlen == SIZE_MAX`, triggering the saved ASan `negative-size-param`.

fine_trace.code: set->postfieldsize = -1;   /* unknown size */
fine_trace.note: Before any fuzzed TLV is applied, libcurl initializes `data->set.postfieldsize` to the sentinel `-1`. That value remains live in this witness because no later `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDSIZE*` setter executes.

Source. On the first parser iteration over the saved 80-byte corpus, these statements decode TLV 1 as `type == 1 (CURLOPT_URL)`, `length == 16`, and `value` pointing at raw bytes `mqtt:/\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff/ `.
When the TLV 1 URL record is handled through the singleton-option path, this helper copies the 16 raw URL bytes into a new 17-byte NUL-terminated string that can be passed to `CURLOPT_URL`.

The `CURLOPT_URL` setter copies the step 3 string into libcurl-owned storage and then aliases that stored string through `data->change.url`, closing the local URL-state transition that later parsing consumes.
On the next TLV iteration, the same parser statements decode TLV 2 as `type == 2 (RESPONSE0)`, `length == 46`, and `value` pointing at staged reply bytes beginning `0x20 0x20 0x00 0x00`.

fine_trace.code: FRESPONSETLV(&fuzz->sockman[0], TLV_TYPE_RESPONSE0, 0);
fine_trace.note: The TLV 2 response record is staged as socket 0's first server reply by storing its decoded `value` pointer and `length` into `responses[0]`.
On the third parser iteration, these statements decode TLV 3 as `type == 5 (CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS)`, `length == 0`, and `value` pointing at the empty tail of the corpus.

For TLV 3, `tlv->length == 0`, so this helper allocates exactly 1 byte and writes only the terminator, producing heap string `""`. The saved ASan allocation stack points here and reports a 1-byte region.

The `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS` setter stores the step 8 empty-string pointer as `data->set.postfields` and switches the configured request method to `HTTPREQ_POST`. This setter does not write `postfieldsize`, so step 1's sentinel `-1` remains unchanged.

Within `curl_url_set(..., data->change.url, ...)`, the absolute URL from step 4 enters `seturl()`. Scanning stops at the slash after the eight `0xff` host bytes, so the remaining suffix `/ ` is copied into the scratch `path` buffer while the `0xff` bytes stay in `hostname`.
The parsed scratch path from step 10 is persisted in the URL handle as `u->path == "/ "`.
Later in the same URL parse, `curl_url_get(...PATH...)` duplicates the parsed handle path from step 11 into `data->state.up.path`, closing the project-side handoff that MQTT later consumes.

fine_trace.code: data->state.httpreq = data->set.method;
fine_trace.note: `Curl_pretransfer()` copies the configured method from step 9 into live transfer state, so `data->state.httpreq == HTTPREQ_POST` when MQTT state handling reaches `mqtt_doing()`.

From the staged response in step 6, `mqtt_doing()` reads control byte `0x20`, then reads remaining-length byte `0x20`; `mqtt_decode_len()` yields 32, so the nonzero branch calls `mqstate(conn, mqtt->nextstate, MQTT_NOSTATE)` and advances out of `MQTT_REMAINING_LENGTH` into the pending `MQTT_CONNACK` handler state.

In the `MQTT_CONNACK` state reached after step 14, `Curl_read(..., readbuf, 2, ...)` pulls the next two staged reply bytes into `readbuf`; on this witness they are `0x00 0x00`, and `nread == 2` so the short-read failure path is skipped.
Because step 15 populated `readbuf` with `0x00 0x00`, this predicate is false and `mqtt_verify_connack()` leaves `result` successful.
With step 16 leaving `result == CURLE_OK` and step 13 having set `state.httpreq` to `HTTPREQ_POST`, `mqtt_doing()` takes the POST arm and enters `mqtt_publish()` rather than `mqtt_subscribe()`.

fine_trace.code:
result = Curl_urldecode(conn->data, path + 1, 0, topic, topiclen,
                            REJECT_NADA);
fine_trace.note: From the parsed URL state in step 12, `path` is `/ ` on this witness. `mqtt_get_topic()` strips the leading slash and decodes the remaining single space into a 1-byte topic, so `topiclen == 1`.

fine_trace.code:
char *payload = conn->data->set.postfields;
size_t payloadlen = (size_t)conn->data->set.postfieldsize;
fine_trace.note: Root cause. `payload` aliases the empty-string pointer from step 9, but `payloadlen` is obtained by casting the still-live sentinel `postfieldsize == -1` from step 1 to `size_t`, producing `SIZE_MAX` instead of the real payload length 0.

fine_trace.code:
remaininglength = payloadlen + 2 + topiclen;
encodelen = mqtt_encode_len(encodedbytes, remaininglength);
fine_trace.note: Using `payloadlen == SIZE_MAX` from step 19 and `topiclen == 1` from step 18, the unsigned addition wraps down to `2`. `mqtt_encode_len()` therefore emits a 1-byte remaining-length encoding for a logically enormous payload.
The wrapped values from step 20 make `malloc()` request only `2 + 1 + 1 = 4` bytes for the entire MQTT PUBLISH packet.

Packet assembly writes the control byte, 1 encoded-length byte, 2 topic-length bytes, and the 1-byte topic from step 18 before any payload copy. After line 353, `i == 5`, so the next destination `&pkt[i]` is already one byte past the 4-byte allocation from step 21.

fine_trace.code: memcpy(&pkt[i], payload, payloadlen);
fine_trace.note: Sink. `payload` still aliases the 1-byte empty string from step 8 through step 9, `payloadlen` is `SIZE_MAX` from step 19, and step 22 already advanced the destination past the tiny packet allocation. AddressSanitizer intercepts this call as `negative-size-param (size=-1)` at `mqtt_publish` line 354 / `__asan_memcpy`.

format.name: curl_fuzzer MQTT TLV corpus
format.contract: Exactly the staged 80-byte `poc`. Direct inspection of the bytes shows exactly three TLVs: TLV 1 `CURLOPT_URL`, length 16, data `mqtt:/\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff/ `; TLV 2 `Server banner (sent on connection)`, length 46, whose first four bytes are `20 20 00 00`; and TLV 3 `CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS`, length 0. That exact combination gives libcurl a parsed MQTT URL whose path is `/ `, stages a CONNACK-accepting mock-server reply, and creates a real 1-byte empty-string payload while leaving `data->set.postfieldsize` at the `Curl_init_userdefined()` default `-1`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger beyond this exact TLV layout and the observed `mqtt_publish()` path.
